{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOUjYZpM8AAAABUha9qg", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BlRsezg-CqN8", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BlRse", "number": 84, "title": "Wait for required human confirmation after PR review instead of repeating fixes", "body": "## Problem

The default GitWeave Task graph routes every unsuccessful PR review through `fix → publish → review`. It does not distinguish a defect that an agent can fix from missing evidence or a decision that requires a human.

For my-audio-to-text #17/#18, agents repeatedly reviewed and updated documentation while required human confirmation remained unavailable. Repeating the fix/publication loop could not supply that confirmation and eventually exhausted the 30-step budget.

ProjectWeave already provides Issue comment/wait commands for pre-implementation readiness. They cannot simply be wired after the current review node: review returns PR/approval/findings data, whereas the readiness commands require status/questions/snapshot data and do not forward PR identity.

## Expected outcome

When PR review determines that human input or confirmation is necessary, request it and wait for a relevant Issue update instead of repeatedly running fix/publication agents. Preserve the PR context and re-review when new information arrives.

Proposed flow:

```text
review
  ├─ approved → existing merge path
  ├─ agent-fixable findings → fix → publish → review
  └─ human confirmation needed → request confirmation → wait
                                                       ↓ Issue updated
                                                     review
```

Implement this through the default graph, review instructions/result schema, and a small Command adapter or extension of the existing readiness commands. The existing GitWeave Runtime supports the required conditionals, loops, schemas, and blocking Command nodes; Runtime changes are not needed for this approach.

- Review must distinguish approval, agent-fixable findings, and human-input blockers. Supply concrete questions/expected confirmation and an Issue snapshot for the human-input path.
- A command posts the request and a command waits for an Issue update without invoking an AI on each poll. Preserve the reviewed baseline across the handoff so a concurrent reply is not lost, and exclude marked automation comments from changes that wake the wait.
- Preserve the PR number, URL, and current reviewed head SHA through request/wait; return the updated snapshot to review. Keep existing head/open-Issue/merge safeguards.
- While waiting, do not call fix/publish/review repeatedly or consume additional graph steps per poll. A new comment is a trigger to reassess, not proof that the requested confirmation has passed; insufficient results return to waiting.
- If both a code defect and a human check remain, fix the agent-fixable problem and then wait for the human result, retaining the updated PR head.
- If the Issue closes while waiting, stop the path without merging or reopening it.
- Preserve existing configured provider/model/effort settings. Document the graph/output changes and how existing generated graphs can adopt them without overwriting user customization.

Add automated regression coverage using local fixtures for: unchanged Issue while polling; sufficient response; insufficient/unrelated response; reply during review/request handoff; Issue closure while waiting; and code-fix-plus-human-input flow with updated PR identity. These checks should not require a real person or physical device.

This Issue adds the resident review-stage wait path. It does not add resource-releasing suspension, a new Runtime pause mechanism, capacity retries, or the withdrawn PR-creation/update split proposal. Existing resident wait/resource/shutdown behavior should be documented accurately.

## Context

An isolated experiment ran the actual GitWeave Runtime and ProjectWeave's existing readiness polling against a local Issue API fixture, with simulated reviewer decisions. It verified all five behavioral cases above and separately confirmed that the existing review output is incompatible without a bridge. During unchanged polling, only one review occurred; no fix/publish calls occurred and graph step count stayed constant. A sufficient answer resumed review with the same PR identity. No real GitHub writes or AI calls were used in that experiment, and production graphs have not been changed.

The experiment validates the control flow and contracts, not the accuracy of an AI deciding whether a human confirmation is necessary. Final implementation should add clear review instructions and checked-in regression tests.

- Existing template: https://github.com/takahirox/projectweave/blob/main/projectweave/templates/gitweave.json
- Existing wait implementation: https://github.com/takahirox/projectweave/blob/main/projectweave/readiness.py
- Observed Tasks: https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/issues/17 and https://github.com/takahirox/my-audio-to-text/issues/18
- Complementary Issue-authoring guidance: https://github.com/takahirox/gitweave/issues/110 (avoid unnecessary human-dependent acceptance criteria). Necessary human checks still need this wait path.
